events.event: The IHSG closed down 3.49% at 5,098.06 on 29 October, near its low of the day, after opening around 5,305 and reversing before 10:00 WIB.
events.key_numbers: IHSG 5,098.06 (-184.26 pts, -3.49%) · open ~5,305.20 · 217.69 million lots, Rp10.13 T traded · utilities -5.99%, basic materials -4.02% · drags: BBCA, ASII, BBRI, TLKM, BMRI
events.why_it_matters: Biggest one-day fall since the 19 Oct slump, wiping out the previous days' recovery and putting the index back near 10-year lows.
events.spreading_evidence: Several CNBC Indonesia breaking items on 29 Oct; Kontan, Kompas, Bisnis all report it

events.event: BCA (BBCA) shares fell 6.35% to Rp4,940 on 29 October, the worst of the big four banks, with the largest foreign net sell among them.
events.key_numbers: BBCA -6.35% to Rp4,940, foreign net sell Rp503.49 B · BBRI -3.77% to Rp2,810, net sell Rp164.50 B · BMRI -3.12% to Rp3,720, net sell Rp155.86 B · BBNI -3.28% to Rp3,240, net sell Rp36.68 B · total foreign net sell Rp1.52 T (body) vs Rp1.08 T (Kontan sidebar)
events.why_it_matters: BCA is the market's heaviest stock and many retail investors hold it, so its drop drives the whole index.

events.event: The US Federal Reserve held rates at 3.75%-4.00% in a split vote, with two officials favouring a hike, and Chair Kevin Warsh declined to signal the next move.
events.key_numbers: Fed funds 3.75%-4.00% · dissent: Lisa Cook and Beth Hammack wanted +25 bp · ~80% market odds of a December hike · US 10-year yield 5.042% · US jobless claims 194,000 vs 200,000 expected
events.why_it_matters: Higher US rates pull money out of Indonesian stocks, bonds and the rupiah, the main reason cited for the 29 Oct sell-off.

events.event: US September PCE inflation rose to 3.6% year on year, with core at 3.1%, both matching forecasts, keeping a Fed hike in play.
events.key_numbers: Headline PCE 3.6% y/y (Aug 3.4%), +0.5% m/m · core PCE 3.1% y/y (Aug 3.0%), +0.3% m/m · savings rate 3.8%
events.why_it_matters: Sticky US inflation means US rates stay high longer, adding pressure on the rupiah and Indonesian markets.

events.event: The rupiah closed stronger on 29 October at about Rp18,137-18,140 per US dollar as the dollar index fell, after weakening to about Rp18,184 the day before.
events.key_numbers: Close Rp18,137 (Okezone) / Rp18,140 (Bisnis), +0.26% · 28 Oct ~Rp18,184 per detikFinance headline (would exceed the 8 Jun close of Rp18,170 Bisnis; unverified) · 27 Oct close Rp18,145
events.why_it_matters: The rupiah is hovering at record-weak levels, which raises prices of imports, fuel and electronics.
events.spreading_evidence: detikFinance rupiah/BI items on front page 28-29 Oct

events.event: Shoe factory PT Parkland World Indonesia (PWI) in Lebak, Banten, completed the layoff of all 1,100 workers on 23 October after its building lease ended and was not renewed.
events.key_numbers: 1,100 workers laid off · ~900 earlier furloughed · staged layoffs from late 2025 to 23 Oct 2026 · South Korean-owned
events.why_it_matters: A large PHK in a labour-intensive sector, while the regent hinted at local interference and the company plans to restart elsewhere.
